TUNING_COMMENT: Honest verdict: tuning did not meaningfully improve the model. The search found a configuration with slightly higher CV Top-1 (5-fold 0.8939 vs 0.8924, +0.15 points), but CV macro-F1 is unchanged (0.9392 vs 0.9392), student-test Top-1 is the same (0.9004 vs 0.9005), and log loss is slightly worse (0.0920 vs 0.0894). The tuned model is also slower (bigger trees, 500 rounds). All 20 trials landed between 0.8775 and 0.8953 (Fig 11), and most were within 0.3 points of each other. Our reading is that the default LightGBM configuration was already near the ceiling these features allow: most remaining errors are reverse-twin and intersection confusions that a per-fix classifier cannot resolve, whatever its hyperparameters. The tuned model is kept as the deployed artifact because it was selected by the pre-declared objective, and its HMM result (Section 5) is within 0.1 points of the untuned model's.
HMM_COMMENT: HMM decoding improved Top-1 accuracy on all 10 student-test trips. Pooled Top-1 rose from 90.04% to 92.51%, continuity rose from 94.49% to 98.16%, and mean route F1 rose from 0.81 (raw argmax arcs) to 0.96. The gains are largest where the classifier flips between a road and its reverse twin or a crossing street (trip 00000056: +3.9 points; trip 00000076: +3.0 points). The HMM helped least on trip 00000007 (+0.4 points), where the classifier was already 94.8% correct and continuity was 99.7%, so there was little to fix. The weakest trip is 00000077 (81.9% after HMM): its errors survive decoding because both readings of the ambiguous stretches are connected routes, so the transition model cannot tell them apart. The Gaussian-emission HMM without a classifier scores 88.71%, which is below even the classifier alone. So the learned emissions, not the decoder by itself, carry most of the accuracy, and the two components are complementary. Every one of the 7 classifiers gains 2.4–8.9 points from the same decoder (table in Section 3.1). Decoding the student-test trips took 0.1–1.5 s per trip. 3 transition steps in 2 trips had no feasible transition and were bridged with the penalty, and 4 route breaks could not be filled by a shortest path.
